description: Cross-language schema content-hash canonicalization parity. Each test case provides a schema whose canonical serialization is sensitive to a known divergence source: float rendering (1.0 vs 1), non-ASCII Unicode in strings/keys, large-integer precision, key ordering, and a plain baseline. SDKs MUST canonicalize each schema and compute its content hash; the hashes are compared CROSS-REPO for byte-for-byte agreement. No `expected` hash is recorded here — each SDK computes it and the harness asserts all three implementations agree. Supports finding A-D-037. See `docs/features/schema-system.md` content-addressable cache and §4.15.

test_cases.note: Exposes float-vs-int rendering divergence: 1.0 must canonicalize identically across SDKs (e.g. JSON `1.0` vs Python `1.0` vs Rust serde `1.0`), not collapse to integer `1`. Trailing-zero and decimal-point handling must agree.

Exposes Unicode normalization and escape-policy divergence: non-ASCII keys/values must serialize byte-identically (UTF-8, no \uXXXX escaping by some SDKs and raw bytes by others). Combining marks, surrogate pairs (emoji), and non-Latin scripts must hash the same.

Exposes large-integer precision divergence: values beyond IEEE-754 double exact range (> 2^53) and u64::MAX must not be coerced to float during canonicalization. 9007199254740993 must stay an exact integer literal across SDKs, not round to 9007199254740992.

Exposes key-ordering divergence: keys are declared in non-lexicographic order at both the top level (zeta/alpha/delta) and nested level (yankee/bravo/mike). Canonicalization MUST sort object keys deterministically (recursively) before hashing, while preserving `required` array order semantics.

Baseline control: a trivially canonical schema with ASCII keys in sorted order and no edge-case values. All SDKs must agree on its hash; a divergence here indicates a fundamental canonicalization-format mismatch rather than an edge-case bug.
